questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which observation is best explained by cohesion between water molecules?
options: Water can be pulled up xylem vessels under tension
questions.answer: Water can be pulled up xylem vessels under tension
questions.hint: Cohesion is attraction between molecules of the same substance.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which polysaccharide has β-1,4 glycosidic bonds that produce straight chains linked by hydrogen bonds?
questions.hint: It is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which level of protein structure is stabilised by interactions between R-groups, such as disulfide bridges and ionic bonds?
questions.hint: It describes the overall three-dimensional folding of a single polypeptide.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes a saturated fatty acid?
options: It always has a cis double bond
It is always liquid at room temperature
It has no carbon–carbon double bonds
It has one carbon–carbon double bond
questions.answer: It has no carbon–carbon double bonds
questions.hint: Saturated means every carbon holds as many hydrogens as possible.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What does it mean that the two strands of DNA are antiparallel?
options: They run in opposite directions, one 5′→3′ and the other 3′→5′
They run in the same direction
questions.answer: They run in opposite directions, one 5′→3′ and the other 3′→5′
questions.hint: Think about the orientation of the sugar-phosphate backbones.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An enzyme-catalysed reaction releases 12 cm³ of oxygen in 4 minutes. Calculate the mean rate in cm³ min⁻¹.
questions.hint: Rate = amount of product ÷ time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the effect of a non-competitive inhibitor on an enzyme-catalysed reaction?
options: Its effect disappears at high substrate concentration
It lowers Vmax, and increasing substrate concentration cannot overcome it
It has no effect on Vmax
questions.answer: It lowers Vmax, and increasing substrate concentration cannot overcome it
questions.hint: It binds away from the active site and changes its shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In end-product inhibition of a metabolic pathway, where does the end product bind?
options: to the DNA coding for the enzyme
to the active site of the last enzyme in the pathway
to the substrate of the first reaction
to an allosteric site on an enzyme early in the pathway
questions.answer: to an allosteric site on an enzyme early in the pathway
questions.hint: The aim is to stop the whole pathway at its start.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the type of nuclear division that produces four genetically different haploid nuclei.
questions.hint: It involves two divisions and crossing over.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which observation supports the endosymbiotic theory for the origin of mitochondria?
options: Mitochondria have their own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA
Mitochondria are produced by the Golgi apparatus
Mitochondria have a cell wall made of cellulose
Mitochondria are found in all prokaryotes
questions.answer: Mitochondria have their own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA
questions.hint: Compare mitochondria with bacteria.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Experiments with sterilised broth in swan-necked flasks provided evidence against which idea?
questions.hint: Microorganisms only appeared when the neck was broken.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which molecule is thought to have been both a store of genetic information and a catalyst in the earliest cells?
questions.hint: Some forms of this molecule act as ribozymes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the enzyme that retroviruses use to make DNA from an RNA template.
questions.hint: Its name describes the opposite of normal transcription.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which feature is shared by all viruses?
options: genetic material enclosed in a protein capsid
questions.answer: genetic material enclosed in a protein capsid
questions.hint: Viruses lack the structures needed for their own metabolism.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens at the end of the lytic cycle of a bacteriophage?
options: The host cell bursts and releases new virus particles
The host cell divides normally for many generations
Viral DNA integrates into the host chromosome
questions.answer: The host cell bursts and releases new virus particles
questions.hint: Lysis means splitting.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss whether viruses should be classified as living organisms.
questions.hint: Compare viruses with the functions of life and with cell theory, then reach a conclusion.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of bond forms between neighbouring water molecules?
questions.hint: Think of the attraction between the slightly positive H of one molecule and the slightly negative O of another.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the monomer that is joined to form starch and glycogen.
questions.hint: It is a hexose monosaccharide.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of reaction joins two monosaccharides to form a disaccharide?
questions.hint: A water molecule is released.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer in water?
options: They form peptide bonds with water
They have hydrophilic phosphate heads and hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails
questions.answer: They have hydrophilic phosphate heads and hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails
questions.hint: Consider which part of the molecule is attracted to water.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the bond that links amino acids in a polypeptide.
questions.hint: It forms between the amine group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.hint: In RNA it pairs with adenine.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A DNA sample contains 22% adenine. What percentage of its bases are cytosine?
questions.hint: Use complementary base pairing: A = T and C = G, and all bases add up to 100%.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain what happens to an enzyme at temperatures well above its optimum.
options: The enzyme is used up in the reaction
The substrate becomes denatured but the enzyme is unchanged
Bonds holding its shape break, the active site changes and the substrate can no longer bind
Molecules move more slowly and collide less
questions.answer: Bonds holding its shape break, the active site changes and the substrate can no longer bind
questions.hint: Think about the tertiary structure of the protein.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes competitive inhibition?
options: The inhibitor permanently destroys the enzyme’s primary structure
The inhibitor increases the rate of the reaction
The inhibitor binds to a site away from the active site
The inhibitor has a similar shape to the substrate and binds to the active site
questions.answer: The inhibitor has a similar shape to the substrate and binds to the active site
questions.hint: Competition is for the same place on the enzyme.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A drawing of a mitochondrion is 30 mm long. The actual length is 15 μm. Calculate the magnification.
questions.hint: Convert both lengths to the same unit, then use image size ÷ actual size.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which structure is found in prokaryotic cells?
options: a nucleus with a nuclear membrane
questions.hint: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the passive movement of water across a partially permeable membrane towards a higher solute concentration.
questions.hint: It does not require energy from ATP.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of membrane transport requires energy from ATP?
questions.hint: Look for movement against a concentration gradient.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.hint: It comes straight after the chromosomes line up at the equator.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a root tip sample of 400 cells, 32 are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
questions.hint: Divide the cells in mitosis by the total number of cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain how the properties of water allow sweating to cool the body.
questions.hint: Think about hydrogen bonds and the energy needed to change state.

bus-hl.topic: Term 1 review: introduction to business and human resources

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which business activity belongs to the tertiary sector?
questions.hint: This sector provides services.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which activity is the best example of the quaternary sector?
questions.hint: This sector is knowledge-based.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A new data protection law forces an online retailer to change how it stores customer information. In a STEEPLE analysis this is a:
questions.hint: Ask what kind of external change caused it.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, a large competitor opening nearby would be classified as:
questions.hint: It is external and potentially harmful.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy involves selling more of existing products in existing markets?
questions.hint: It is the lowest-risk quadrant.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a typical example of stakeholder conflict?
options: Suppliers want to be paid on time
Shareholders want higher dividends while employees want higher wages
Customers and shareholders both want the firm to survive
questions.answer: Shareholders want higher dividends while employees want higher wages
questions.hint: Look for two groups whose aims compete for the same resources.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A supermarket chain gets lower unit costs by ordering in very large quantities. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Think about bulk buying.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm had an average workforce of 70 and 14 employees left during the year. Calculate the labour turnover rate (%).
questions.hint: Leavers ÷ average workforce × 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is delayering?
options: Adding new layers of middle management
Removing one or more levels of hierarchy from an organisation
Reducing the number of products sold
questions.answer: Removing one or more levels of hierarchy from an organisation
questions.hint: Think of the shape of the organisation chart.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which leadership style involves the leader making decisions without consulting employees?
questions.hint: Power is concentrated in one person.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: When two firms with very different values and ways of working merge, the resulting problems are known as:
questions.hint: It relates to organisational culture.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Name the form of industrial action in which employees collectively stop working.
questions.hint: It is the most extreme form of collective action.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is meant by a “work-to-rule”?
options: Managers lock employees out of the workplace
Employees do only the minimum required by their contracts
questions.answer: Employees do only the minimum required by their contracts
questions.hint: Rules are followed exactly, and nothing more.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial reward?
questions.hint: It does not involve money.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the IB command term “discuss” require?
options: The precise meaning of a term
A considered and balanced review including a range of arguments, ending with a conclusion
questions.answer: A considered and balanced review including a range of arguments, ending with a conclusion
questions.hint: It is typical of 10-mark questions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain how a culture clash after a merger could affect employee motivation. [4]
questions.hint: Consider values, ways of working and how staff feel about change.

bus-sl.topic: Term 1 review: introduction to business and human resources

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In which sector of the economy does manufacturing take place?
questions.hint: It involves turning raw materials into finished goods.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which business activity belongs to the primary sector?
questions.hint: This sector extracts natural resources.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, what does the letter T stand for?
questions.hint: It is an external factor that could harm the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which elements of a SWOT analysis are internal to the business?
questions.hint: Internal factors are under the firm’s control.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors in a STEEPLE analysis?
questions.hint: List the seven letters and what each represents.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to the Ansoff matrix, selling existing products in new markets is called:
questions.hint: The product stays the same; the customers change.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy usually carries the highest risk?
questions.hint: It combines two unknowns.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy involves launching new products in existing markets?
questions.hint: The customers stay the same.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an internal stakeholder?
questions.hint: Internal stakeholders are members of the organisation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which feature describes a privately held company?
options: It is owned by the government
Owners have limited liability and shares are not sold to the general public
Shares are traded on the stock exchange
questions.answer: Owners have limited liability and shares are not sold to the general public
questions.hint: Think about who can buy the shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the main aim of a social enterprise?
options: To be run by the government
To achieve social or environmental goals, reinvesting most of its surplus
questions.answer: To achieve social or environmental goals, reinvesting most of its surplus
questions.hint: Profit is a means, not the end.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In motivation theory, which of these is a hygiene factor rather than a motivator?
questions.hint: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction but do not motivate on their own.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the likely effect of widening managers’ spans of control?
options: A taller structure with more levels
A flatter organisational structure with fewer levels of hierarchy
questions.answer: A flatter organisational structure with fewer levels of hierarchy
questions.hint: Each manager now supervises more people.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business employed an average of 80 workers last year and 12 left. Calculate the labour turnover rate (%).
questions.hint: Divide the number who left by the average number employed, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the IB command term “define” require?
options: Break down to bring out the essential elements
Give the precise meaning of a word, phrase or concept
Give a balanced review with a conclusion
Give a detailed account including reasons
questions.answer: Give the precise meaning of a word, phrase or concept
questions.hint: It is usually worth 2 marks.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two advantages of a flat organisational structure for a small business. [4]
questions.hint: Think about communication and the cost of management.

chem-hl.topic: Review: atomic structure, the mole and bonding

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which subatomic particle determines the identity of an element?
questions.hint: Think about what the atomic number counts.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the type of bonding present in solid sodium chloride.
questions.hint: Consider a metal combined with a non-metal.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of chromium (Z = 24)?
questions.hint: Chromium is an exception: a half-filled sub-level gives extra stability.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Chlorine consists of 75.78% chlorine-35 (mass 34.97) and 24.22% chlorine-37 (mass 36.97). Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Multiply each isotopic mass by its fractional abundance and add.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of water in 9.00 g of H₂O (Mr = 18.02). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use n = m / M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Methane burns completely: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Calculate the mass, in g, of CO₂ (Mr = 44.01) formed from 0.250 mol of CH₄. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use the mole ratio of CH₄ to CO₂ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 4.0 mol of H₂ react with 3.0 mol of O₂. Determine the maximum amount, in mol, of water formed.
questions.hint: Identify the limiting reactant before using the ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the concentration, in mol dm⁻³, of a solution containing 0.0500 mol of NaOH in 250 cm³ of solution.
questions.hint: Convert the volume to dm³ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the volume, in dm³, occupied by 0.200 mol of an ideal gas at STP (molar volume 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Multiply the amount by the molar volume.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the shape of an ammonia (NH₃) molecule?
questions.hint: Count the bonding pairs and the lone pair around nitrogen.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethene, C₂H₄?
questions.hint: Each carbon has three electron domains.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds are in ethyne, C₂H₂?
questions.hint: A triple bond contains one σ bond; each single bond is one σ bond.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which explains why the first ionisation energy of oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen?
options: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 2p orbital
Oxygen has a smaller nuclear charge
The electron is removed from a 2s orbital in oxygen
Oxygen has an extra inner shell of electrons
questions.answer: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 2p orbital
questions.hint: Compare the 2p orbital diagrams of the two atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which molecule is non-polar even though it contains polar bonds?
questions.hint: Think about whether the bond dipoles cancel because of the shape.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why diamond has a much higher melting point than iodine.
questions.hint: Compare the forces that must be overcome in a giant structure and in a molecular solid.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain how the successive ionisation energies of an element provide evidence for the existence of electron shells.
questions.hint: Look for the large jumps and think about distance from the nucleus.

chem-sl.topic: Review: atomic structure, the mole and bonding

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have different numbers of which particle?
questions.hint: The atomic number stays the same.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of sodium-23 (atomic number 11)?
questions.hint: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the electron configuration of sulfur (Z = 16)?
questions.hint: Fill sub-levels in order until 16 electrons are placed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Lines in the visible region of the hydrogen emission spectrum come from electron transitions down to which energy level?
questions.hint: Transitions to n = 1 release more energy, in the ultraviolet.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the molar mass, in g mol⁻¹, of CaCO₃ (Ca = 40.08, C = 12.01, O = 16.00). Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Remember there are three oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of CaCO₃ (M = 100.09 g mol⁻¹) in 5.00 g. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use n = m / M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
questions.hint: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass, then find the simplest ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. How many mol of HCl react exactly with 0.150 mol of Na₂CO₃?
questions.hint: Use the coefficients in the equation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 8.00 g and the actual yield is 6.40 g. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Divide actual by theoretical and multiply by 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 50.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl is diluted with water to 500 cm³. Calculate the new concentration in mol dm⁻³.
questions.hint: The amount of solute does not change on dilution.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What are the shape and bond angle of a methane (CH₄) molecule?
questions.hint: Four bonding pairs repel as far apart as possible in three dimensions.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which intermolecular force mainly explains why water has a much higher boiling point than hydrogen sulfide?
questions.hint: Oxygen is far more electronegative than sulfur.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Name the type of bond formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons.
questions.hint: It usually forms between two non-metal atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why can solid metals conduct electricity?
questions.hint: Think about the 'sea' in the metallic bonding model.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which substance has a giant covalent structure?
questions.hint: Look for a network of atoms joined by covalent bonds, not small molecules.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why sodium chloride conducts electricity when molten but not when solid.
questions.hint: Think about whether the charged particles can move in each state.

comp-hl.topic: Review: programming fundamentals and computer systems

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure works on a last in, first out (LIFO) basis?
questions.hint: Picture a pile of plates.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which binary number is equal to denary 45?
questions.hint: Use place values 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 2F to denary.
questions.hint: Each hex digit is worth 16 times the one to its right; F = 15.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many different values can be represented using 8 bits?
questions.hint: Each extra bit doubles the number of combinations.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of a NOR gate when both inputs are 0? Answer 0 or 1.
questions.hint: NOR is the inverse of OR.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which CPU register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.hint: Its value increments during each fetch.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of primary memory is volatile?
questions.hint: Volatile means contents are lost when power is removed.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
X = 1
loop COUNT from 1 to 4
    X = X * 2
end loop
output X
questions.hint: Record X after each pass of the loop in a trace table.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
A = 10
B = 3
loop while A > B
    A = A - B
end loop
output A
questions.hint: Check the condition before every repetition.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which programming construct chooses between two paths depending on a condition?
questions.hint: Think of an if–then–else.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement describes a compiler?
options: It translates the whole source code into machine code before execution
It translates and executes one line at a time
It converts assembly code into high-level code
It manages memory while programs run
questions.answer: It translates the whole source code into machine code before execution
questions.hint: Consider when the translation happens.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why does an operating system use virtual memory?
options: To use secondary storage as an extension of RAM
To speed up the network connection
questions.answer: To use secondary storage as an extension of RAM
questions.hint: It helps when RAM is full.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In memory management, what is paging?
options: Dividing memory into fixed-size blocks that can be swapped
Printing memory contents to a file
questions.answer: Dividing memory into fixed-size blocks that can be swapped
questions.hint: Compare it with variable-sized segments.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An array NAMES has 10 elements, indexed from 0. What is the index of the last element?
questions.hint: Indexing starts at zero.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one advantage of distributing a finished program as compiled code rather than as source code to be interpreted.
questions.hint: Think about speed and what the user receives.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe the purpose of a trace table when testing an algorithm.
questions.hint: Consider how it records variables step by step.

comp-sl.topic: Review: programming fundamentals and computer systems

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure works on a first in, first out (FIFO) basis?
questions.hint: Picture people waiting in line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert denary 255 to hexadecimal.
questions.hint: 255 is the largest value one byte can hold.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An image is 100 × 100 pixels with a colour depth of 8 bits. Calculate its size in bytes, ignoring metadata.
questions.hint: Find the number of pixels, then think about how many bytes one 8-bit pixel needs.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of an AND gate when input A = 1 and input B = 0? Answer 0 or 1.
questions.hint: AND needs both inputs to be 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs are different?
questions.hint: It is called 'exclusive'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the role of the ALU in the CPU?
options: It performs arithmetic and logical operations
It stores the next instruction address
It controls the timing of components
questions.answer: It performs arithmetic and logical operations
questions.hint: Look at the words in its full name.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is secondary storage?
questions.hint: Secondary storage keeps data when the power is off.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
TOTAL = 0
loop N from 1 to 5
    if N mod 2 = 0 then
        TOTAL = TOTAL + N
    end if
end loop
output TOTAL
questions.hint: Only add N when it is even.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
COUNT = 0
NUMS = [4, 9, 2, 7, 5]
loop I from 0 to 4
    if NUMS[I] > 4 then
        COUNT = COUNT + 1
    end if
end loop
output COUNT
questions.hint: Count only the values greater than 4.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which construct repeats a block of code as long as a condition is true?
questions.hint: It is a form of iteration.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure stores a fixed number of elements of the same type, accessed by an index?
questions.hint: Think of NAMES[3].

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is a main function of an operating system?
options: Managing hardware resources such as memory and the CPU
questions.answer: Managing hardware resources such as memory and the CPU
questions.hint: It sits between the user's applications and the hardware.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name for a named value that cannot change while a program is running?
questions.hint: It is the opposite of a variable.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why computers represent data in binary.
questions.hint: Think about the two states of electronic switches.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe two differences between RAM and ROM.
questions.hint: Consider volatility and whether the contents can be changed.
